FULL TEXT:
National Law University and Judicial
Academy, Assam
Call for Applications for Entry-Level Lawyers in Assam
Applications are invited from eligible early-career Lawyers in Assam for the
forthcoming cohort of the Continuing Legal Education (CLE) Programme — a
Six Month, field-embedded Programme offered by the National Law University
and Judicial Academy (NLUJA), Assam, in collaboration with the Azim Premji
Foundation.
About the Programme
The Continuing Legal Education (CLE) Programme is designed to strengthen the
professional capacity of early-career lawyers and enhance access to quality, rights-
based legal services across Assam. The programme will provide recently qualified
lawyers with structured learning, practical exposure, professional mentoring, and
opportunities to engage with real-world legal and community issues.
The CLE curriculum will cover key areas of legal practice, including criminal
justice, gender laws, education and health rights, land and property law, procedural
law, legal drafting, professional ethics, and the use of legal technology. Classroom-
based learning will be complemented by field assignments, exposure visits to
courts, jails, and public institutions, as well as collaborative engagements with civil
society organisations and NGOs. This blended approach will enable participants to
connect legal knowledge with practical challenges encountered.
The programme will primarily focus on lawyers from geographically remote
districts of Assam, with particular attention to tribal and hill areas. Young lawyers
working in these areas often have limited opportunities for structured professional
mentoring and continuing legal education.
By building locally rooted legal capacity, the programme seeks to support a new
generation of advocates who are equipped to understand and respond to region-
specific legal challenges while remaining grounded in constitutional values and
statutory frameworks. It aims to foster practical legal competence, analytical
thinking, ethical practice, and socially responsive approaches.
Ultimately, the CLE Programme seeks to contribute to a stronger and more
accessible local justice ecosystem by enabling young advocates to provide
effective, informed, and rights-based legal services and to respond meaningfully to
the needs of individuals and communities within their respective districts.
At a glance
Who Early-career lawyers who have recently completed
their legal education
Where Fresh Law Graduate/Practicing in Assam
Duration Six months, field-embedded (with in-person
intensives at NLUJA, Assam)
Cohort 20 Law graduate selected across the state
Mode Blended — field placement + periodic in-person
blocks + weekly online sessions
Award Certificate from NLUJA, Assam, with an end-line
impact brief
Who should apply — eligibility
You are eligible to apply if you meet all of the following:
● Freshers (Law Graduate) / Freshers enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar
Council. (0 – 2 years of experience)
● Able to commit to the full Six-months tenure, including in-person
intensive blocks at NLUJA, Assam.
Preference will be given to young and early-career lawyers who have recently
completed their legal education..
What Trainees will do
● Attend structured training sessions on criminal justice, gender laws,
education and health rights, land and property law, procedural law,
legal drafting, ethics, and legal technology.
● Participate in practical exercises, case discussions, simulations, and
problem-solving sessions based on real-life legal issues.
● Undertake field-based assignments to understand legal and justice-related
challenges within their communities.
● Visit courts, jails, legal aid institutions, government offices, and other
public institutions to gain practical exposure to the justice system.
● Work collaboratively with NGOs and civil society organisations on
community-focused legal issues.
● Develop skills in legal research, drafting, advocacy, documentation, and
use of digital legal resources.
● Engage with issues relating to customary practices, Sixth Schedule
governance, land and resource disputes, and access to justice relevant to
their regions.
● Receive professional mentoring and peer-learning opportunities from
experienced lawyers and practitioners.
● Apply their learning to their own practice and contribute to providing
accessible, ethical, and rights-based legal services to individuals and
communities in their respective districts.
What Trainees receive
● Intensive, structured mentorship from a senior mentor (a High Court / Senior
Advocate).
● Exposure to complex casework and a cross-jurisdictional network of
practitioners across the State.
● A Certificate from NLUJA, Assam, with an end-line impact brief; an
optional letter of recommendation for those completing with distinction.
● Advanced workshops and access to NLUJA's academic resources and legal
databases during in-person blocks.
● Accommodation for in-person blocks — to be paid as per project
guidelines.
Representation & equity
The Continuing Legal Education (CLE) Programme is committed to a fair and
inclusive cohort. At least 40% of trainees will be women, and at least 30% will be
drawn from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other marginalised
backgrounds. Selection also gives attention to geographical balance across
districts.
Selection process
● Submit your application through the official Email-Id (see 'How to apply').
● Application dossier: a self-authored writing sample, and a statement of
purpose.
● Shortlisting on the basis of prior commitment to legal aid, rights-based
advocacy or community engagement.
● Two-stage interview — one online and one in-person — before a panel of
NLUJA Assam.
Apply online
E-mail ID: registrar@nluassam.ac.in
Send all the required documents, and submit before the deadline. (03 October
2026)
What to prepare
Keep the following ready before you begin — you will upload them in the portal:
● A statement of purpose (500–800 words) on why you seek the training and
what you hope to achieve.
● A self-authored writing sample (a pleading, legal opinion, article or note).
Anonymise all client-identifying details.
● Your curriculum vitae, Bar enrolment certificate (if available), law degree, a
government photo ID, and — if applicable — category / disability
certificates.
How to apply
Applications are accepted only through E-mail:

Applications open 23 September 2026
Last date to apply 03 October 2026
Online interaction To be notified to the concerned.
In-person interview To be notified to the concerned.
Orientation &
commencement
November 2026 (Tentative)
Dates are indicative and will be confirmed on the portal. Please check the portal for
updates.
Contact
Registrar Office, National Law University and Judicial Academy, Assam, Hajo
Road, Amingaon, Guwahati – 781031, Assam.
Phone: +91-361-2738891 Email: registrar@nluassam.ac.in
Important notes
● All information and documents submitted must be true and correct;
misrepresentation will lead to disqualification.
● Client confidentiality must be maintained — anonymise all client data in
writing samples and case histories.
● The Continuing Legal Education (CLE) is an equal-opportunity programme;
applications from women, persons with disabilities and candidates from
marginalized communities are especially encouraged.
